title: Air Preheater

introduction.definition: An air preheater transfers heat from the boiler flue gas to the incoming combustion air. In the rotary regenerative (Ljungström) type, a slowly rotating rotor packed with corrugated steel plates passes alternately through the gas and air streams: the plates absorb heat in the gas and release it to the air.
applications: Coal, oil and gas-fired utility boilers
key_points: Hotter air → better combustion and efficiency
Air-to-gas leakage through seals is the main loss
Cold end prone to acid corrosion/fouling
introduction.summary: A rotary regenerative air preheater transfers heat from boiler flue gas to the incoming combustion air. A large rotor packed with corrugated steel plates turns slowly; the plates are heated while passing through the gas side and release that heat while passing through the air side.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Air outlet temperature rises with gas inlet temperature and rotor speed up to a limit; leakage % rises as seals wear.

temperature.title: Hot side vs cold side of the rotor
temperature.description: The matrix plates in the gas half (right) are heated by the flue gas; as the rotor turns (about 1–3 rpm) they move into the air half (left) and give that heat to the combustion air. Hotter combustion air improves boiler efficiency (roughly 1 % fuel saving per ~20 °C of extra air temperature, rule of thumb). Leakage of air into gas past the seals is the main performance loss.

foundation: Level concrete plinth/foundation designed for operating weight full of water; allow access for tube cleaning and burner maintenance.
alignment: Level the boiler; align burner and fan; check expansion allowances on headers and casings.
piping: Fit safety valves with unobstructed discharge piped to a safe place; feedwater with check and isolation valves; blowdown to a blowdown vessel.
Flue/stack sized for the draught required; explosion relief where specified.
commissioning: Boil-out/chemical clean; hydro-test; set and test safety valves; test low-water cut-outs and flame safeguard (purge, ignition, flame failure); tune combustion (O₂, CO).

symptoms: Higher fan power, O₂ rise across heater

remedies: Raise cold-end temperature; wash; enamelled baskets

safety: Fire risk from deposits — fire detection and washing systems; lock out the drive before entry.

video_tutorials.title: Air Preheater — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Air Preheater.
An air preheater transfers heat from the boiler flue gas to the incoming combustion air.

In the rotary regenerative (Ljungström) type, a slowly rotating rotor packed with corrugated steel plates passes alternately through the gas and air streams: the plates absorb heat in the gas and release it to the air.
Typical applications include coal, oil and gas-fired utility boilers; large industrial boilers and furnaces.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Housing (rotor shell), Rotor with Heating-Element Baskets (matrix) — turns slowly through gas and air.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Air Preheater — Operation

script.narration: How the Air Preheater works.
Hot flue gas passes down through one half of the rotor.
The rotor turns slowly, carrying heated plates to the air side.
Combustion air flows up through the other half and is heated.
Seals and sector plates limit leakage between the streams.
The drive turns the rotor through a pinion and pin rack.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The matrix plates in the gas half (right) are heated by the flue gas; as the rotor turns (about 1–3 rpm) they move into the air half (left) and give that heat to the combustion air.

video_tutorials.title: Air Preheater — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Air Preheater.
Monitor ΔP, leakage (O₂ rise) and temperatures.
Soot blowing/washing of the matrix.
Adjust/replace seals; replace cold-end baskets.
Watch for high air-to-gas leakage: higher fan power, O₂ rise across heater. Common cause: seal wear, rotor distortion.
Watch for cold-end fouling/corrosion: ΔP rise. Common cause: acid condensation, ammonium bisulphate.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
